newsitem.title: GERMANY: Weekly German intervention grain offers detailed.
newsitem.headline: Weekly German intervention grain offers detailed.

text.p: Sales offers into German grain intervention stores in the November-May 1996/97 season continued to lag those in the same 1995/96 period, figures from the state grain intervention board BLE showed on Monday.
Volumes as of January 31 totalled 458,851 tonnes compared with 1,317,697 tonnes a year earlier.
The figure described volumes accepted, but not yet delivered to stores, by the close last Friday.
Free market bread wheat and rye prices were well above the February intervention buying-in price of 241.52 marks a tonne, traders said.
But feed rye and barley prices were heading towards intervention because ample feed wheat supplies dominated the feed grain market, they added.
